steps.name: Define domain entities and value objects
steps.description: Create pure TypeScript domain entities (Item, Wardrobe, StyleProfile, Outfit, WearEvent) and value objects (Color, Size, Occasion, Season, Category, WeatherContext, AIClassification, WardrobeStats). No external imports in packages/domain. Business rules BR-01, BR-03, BR-04, BR-05, BR-06, BR-09 enforced in entities.
criteria: Item entity holds all fields from data-models.md schema including status lifecycle (active, pending_ai, pending_review, deleted)
Outfit suggestion request returns null when wardrobe item_count < 5
Outfit item composition is immutable after construction; attempting modification raises error
WearEvent created only with an explicit outfit reference and final items list (BR-05)
StyleProfile with calibration_completed=false returns archetype=classic, occasion_priorities=[work,casual], palette=neutral when queried
All value objects are immutable; equality is structural, not reference-based
packages/domain has zero imports from AWS SDK, Supabase, Axios, or any framework
steps.implementation_notes: WardrobeStats is a value object derived at query time — never instantiate from a DB row. All entity fields must be readonly. Use a fast TypeScript-native test framework for unit tests.
quality_gates: TypeScript compilation passes with strict mode and zero type errors in packages/domain
dependency-cruiser passes with zero violations — no external imports in packages/domain
All entity fields annotated as readonly compile without mutation errors

steps.name: Define outbound port interfaces
steps.description: Declare all outbound port interfaces in packages/domain/src/ports/outbound/. Covers persistence ports (Item, Wardrobe, Outfit, WearEvent, StyleProfile repositories) and service ports (AIProcessor, WeatherService, ImageStore, ConsentLog). Interfaces only — no implementations.
criteria: ItemRepositoryPort declares save, findById, findByWardrobe, delete, and findByOccasionAndSeason operations
WardrobeRepositoryPort declares findByUserId and updateItemCount operations
AIProcessorPort declares processImage returning AIClassification and background-removed URL
WeatherServicePort declares fetchForecast returning WeatherContext or null on failure
ConsentLogPort declares logConsent and isConsentGranted for photo storage consent (GDPR)
All port interfaces reference only domain types — zero external library types in signatures
Each port file exports exactly one interface; no implementation code
steps.implementation_notes: WeatherServicePort returns null (not throw) when forecast unavailable — graceful degradation is a domain contract. ConsentLogPort checked at use-case level before ImageStorePort. OutfitRepositoryPort must support date-window queries for BR-04 rotation check.
quality_gates: TypeScript compilation passes with strict mode and zero type errors
All port interfaces import only from packages/domain — dependency-cruiser passes
WeatherServicePort return type explicitly includes null variant
Port contract test file compiles with mock implementations satisfying all interface shapes

steps.name: Implement inbound use cases
steps.description: Implement CalibrateStyleUseCase, DigitizeItemUseCase, and SuggestOutfitUseCase. Each receives port interfaces via constructor injection. No adapter imports in use case files.
criteria: CalibrateStyleUseCase.skipCalibration produces StyleProfile with BR-09 defaults persisted via StyleProfileRepositoryPort
DigitizeItemUseCase.confirmItem increments Wardrobe item_count only after save succeeds — pending items excluded (BR-06 enforced: photo_url references background-removed version)
DigitizeItemUseCase.correctMetadata logs correction via AIQualityLogPort with predicted and corrected categories
SuggestOutfitUseCase.getDailyOutfit returns null when item_count < 5 (BR-01), enforces >= 3 items per outfit (BR-03), and skips combinations seen within rotation window (BR-04)
SuggestOutfitUseCase.getDailyOutfit proceeds without WeatherContext when WeatherServicePort returns null — outfit is still returned
SuggestOutfitUseCase.acceptOutfit creates WearEvent with final item IDs — does not mutate OutfitSuggestion (BR-05)
Outfit status is set to invalidated when any referenced item_id is deleted from wardrobe (BR-08)
steps.implementation_notes: Use constructor injection for all port dependencies. Use hand-rolled in-memory stubs for ports — no framework mocking at this layer. BR-04 rotation window: 7 days (>= 15 items) or 3 days (< 15 items). Keep use case orchestration thin — domain logic lives in entities.
quality_gates: Vitest unit tests cover all three use cases with 100% of business rules BR-01 through BR-10
SuggestOutfitUseCase returns outfit when WeatherServicePort stub returns null
DigitizeItemUseCase.confirmItem test: item_count does not increment until repository save resolves
CalibrateStyleUseCase.skipCalibration test: persisted profile matches BR-09 defaults exactly
All use case tests run without any database, HTTP, or file system access

steps.name: Implement in-memory and mock adapters
steps.description: Build in-memory adapter implementations of all outbound ports for unit and integration tests: InMemoryItemRepository, InMemoryWardrobeRepository, InMemoryStyleProfileRepository, InMemoryOutfitRepository, MockAIProcessor, MockWeatherService. These are the only adapters wired during the walking-skeleton integration test.
criteria: InMemoryItemRepository satisfies ItemRepositoryPort and stores items in a Map keyed by item_id
InMemoryWardrobeRepository satisfies WardrobeRepositoryPort and maintains item_count consistently with item inserts and deletes
MockAIProcessor returns a configurable AIClassification — callers can set return value per test scenario
MockWeatherService is configurable to return a WeatherContext or null to test graceful degradation
All in-memory adapters reset state between tests without process restart
InMemoryConsentLogAdapter records consent events and exposes a query for test assertion
steps.implementation_notes: Adapters must satisfy their port interface type exactly — TypeScript enforces this at compile time. MockAIProcessor supports scenario-based configuration to drive Cucumber step definitions. Adapters live in packages/domain to avoid circular dependencies.
quality_gates: TypeScript compilation confirms each adapter class satisfies its port interface
Vitest: each adapter test covers save, find, update, and delete operations
MockWeatherService test: returns null when configured to simulate API failure
MockAIProcessor test: returns the configured classification without HTTP calls

steps.name: Implement Supabase persistence adapters
steps.description: Build SupabaseItemRepository and SupabaseWardrobeRepository implementing their port interfaces. Includes the PostgreSQL schema migration for all MVP tables. Integration tests target a local Supabase instance.
criteria: SupabaseItemRepository.save writes a row to the items table and returns a domain Item with all fields populated
SupabaseItemRepository.findByOccasionAndSeason returns only active items matching provided occasion and season arrays
SupabaseWardrobeRepository.findByUserId returns the wardrobe with current item_count maintained by DB trigger
Database migration creates all tables from data-models.md with correct indexes: (user_id, status), (user_id, occasions, seasons, status), (user_id, suggestion_date DESC)
Integration tests run against supabase start (local) — no production credentials in CI
SupabaseItemRepository maps DB rows to domain Item entities; no raw DB types escape the adapter boundary
steps.implementation_notes: Supabase client inside adapters only — never in domain code. item_count maintained by DB trigger on INSERT/DELETE. Run supabase db reset before integration tests. Map Supabase error codes to domain-level exceptions at the adapter boundary.
quality_gates: supabase db push --local succeeds with migration 001_initial_schema.sql
Integration test: SupabaseItemRepository.save then findById returns identical domain entity
Integration test: item_count on wardrobe increments after item insert and decrements after status=deleted update
Integration test: findByOccasionAndSeason excludes pending_ai and deleted items
No Supabase types or client instances referenced outside packages/functions/src/adapters/
ai_quality_log table records corrected vs predicted category per item confirmation; correction rate queryable per category (BR-10)

steps.name: Implement Nano Banana AI adapter
steps.description: Build NanaBananaAdapter implementing AIProcessorPort. Accepts a photo upload key, calls Nano Banana API for background removal and garment classification, returns an AIClassification value object. Invoked by Lambda consumer via SQS — not synchronously from HTTP handlers.
criteria: NanaBananaAdapter.processImage calls the Nano Banana API with the photo key and returns an AIClassification within the 10-second P95 target
Adapter maps Nano Banana response fields to domain AIClassification value object — no Nano Banana types escape the adapter
When Nano Banana returns a non-2xx response, adapter throws a classifiable domain error (not an HTTP error)
Adapter includes retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (5xx responses, network timeouts)
When Nano Banana API is unavailable for multiple retries, adapter returns domain error allowing item to enter pending_review state
Background-removed image URL stored in AIClassification.photoUrl references the CDN URL, not an S3 raw path (BR-06)
steps.implementation_notes: Use HTTP client with configurable timeout to meet 10s P95 SLA. Implement circuit breaker pattern; software-crafter chooses implementation approach. Mock the Nano Banana HTTP endpoint in tests via HTTP interception library — no real API calls in CI.
quality_gates: Vitest: adapter test with msw stub returns populated AIClassification for a 200 response
Vitest: adapter test returns domain error (not HTTP error) on Nano Banana 503 response
Vitest: circuit breaker test — adapter opens after 3 consecutive 503s and returns error without calling API again
TypeScript: NanaBananaAdapter implements AIProcessorPort — compilation verifies interface compliance

steps.name: Wire use cases and adapters via dependency injection
steps.description: Create the DI container wiring use cases to adapter implementations. For the walking skeleton, wire to Supabase adapters for persistence and mock adapters for AI and weather. Run walking-skeleton.feature Cucumber scenario end-to-end.
criteria: The DI container produces a fully wired CalibrateStyleUseCase, DigitizeItemUseCase, and SuggestOutfitUseCase with no missing dependencies
The walking-skeleton.feature @smoke scenario passes end-to-end against local Supabase and mock AI/weather adapters
CalibrateStyleUseCase receives SupabaseStyleProfileRepository; DigitizeItemUseCase receives MockAIProcessor and SupabaseItemRepository; SuggestOutfitUseCase receives MockWeatherService
The DI container is environment-configurable — a test profile uses in-memory/mock adapters; a production profile uses Supabase/Nano Banana adapters
No use case class imports adapter implementations directly — all wiring occurs in the container
steps.implementation_notes: Use a simple factory function pattern — no IoC framework needed at this scale. container.ts is the only file that references both domain use cases and adapter implementations. Cucumber step definitions import the container and call use case methods.
quality_gates: cucumber-js --tags @smoke on walking-skeleton.feature exits 0 with all steps green
Container test: swapping MockAIProcessor for NanaBananaAdapter requires only a container change — no use case file changes
No circular imports: dependency-cruiser passes on packages/functions/src/container.ts
Walking skeleton scenario completes in under 30 seconds (local Supabase + mock adapters)

steps.name: Validate acceptance tests against local Supabase and mock adapters
steps.description: Run all @smoke scenarios across milestone-1, milestone-2, and milestone-3 feature files against the wired system. Write missing Cucumber step definitions to achieve full @smoke coverage.
criteria: All @smoke scenarios in milestone-1-style-calibration.feature pass: style calibration complete, skip with defaults, profile persisted
All @smoke scenarios in milestone-2-item-digitization.feature pass: photo processed, item_count increments only on confirm, correction logged
All @smoke scenarios in milestone-3-outfit-unlock.feature pass: celebration triggers at item 5, progress indicator accurate, outfit contains >= 3 items (BR-03)
No @smoke scenario produces a pending or skipped result — all have implemented step definitions
Outfit returned by SuggestOutfitUseCase in milestone-3 scenarios contains only items from the test wardrobe
steps.implementation_notes: The Cucumber World object holds container instance and test state between steps. Step definitions call use case methods from the container — no direct DB queries. Each scenario resets Supabase state via beforeEach hook scoped to the test user. Milestone-4 @smoke scenarios are not required to pass in this step.
quality_gates: cucumber-js --tags '@smoke and @milestone_1' exits 0 with all scenarios green
cucumber-js --tags '@smoke and @milestone_2' exits 0 with all scenarios green
cucumber-js --tags '@smoke and @milestone_3' exits 0 with all scenarios green
No step definition is marked as pending for any @smoke scenario across milestones 1-3
Test run completes in under 60 seconds on local Supabase
